steps: Load analysis/delta_by_size.csv.
Create predictor X = numpy.log2(size) (7 values) and response Y = delta_mean; fit OLS using scipy.stats.linregress or statsmodels.OLS; extract intercept a, slope b, R², p-value, and 95% CI for slope.

Compute N_star = 2**(-a/b); if b >= 0, set N_star_note='no_crossover_positive_slope'; if N_star < 500, set N_star_note='extrapolated_below_range'; if N_star > 60000, set N_star_note='extrapolated_above_range'; else set N_star_note='within_tested_range'.

Run 5000-iteration bootstrap: for each iteration, resample 7 (X,Y) pairs with replacement, fit OLS, compute N_star_boot = 2**(-a_boot/b_boot) (clip to [1,1e9] to handle degenerate fits); collect into a list.
Compute bootstrap 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles as 95% CI; save 5000-row distribution to analysis/bootstrap_N_star.csv with columns: iter, N_star_boot.

title: How Augmentation Benefit Scales with Training Set Size for a Small CNN on Fashion-MNIST

agents.name: ML Engineer
agents.instructions: You implement and test deep learning code. Write src/train_fmnist.py as a self-contained importable module exporting SmallCNN, get_transforms(), train_one_epoch(), evaluate_accuracy(), and a CLI entry point. Ensure the CNN architecture exactly matches the spec: two conv blocks with BN, Dropout, MaxPool; a head with 256 units. Write config/config.json with all hyperparameters. Run a quick forward-pass test to confirm the model produces (batch,10) outputs before declaring success. Keep code clean, modular, and importable by GPU job scripts.

agents.name: Data Engineer
agents.instructions: You prepare reproducible datasets for machine learning experiments. Download Fashion-MNIST via torchvision, extract training labels, and apply stratified sampling for all 7 training sizes (500,1000,2500,5000,10000,30000,60000) with seeds 42 and 123, using a 90/10 train/val split. Save index arrays to data/subset_indices.npz. Verify and log per-class counts for the two smallest sizes to data/class_balance_check.txt, asserting ±1 balance tolerance per class at N=500.

agents.name: GPU Training Engineer
agents.instructions: You orchestrate GPU training experiments. Write self-contained GPU job scripts that install their own dependencies, import src/train_fmnist.py, load subset_indices.npz, and run all required configurations, saving results incrementally to CSV after each run. Use run_gpu_jobs with 90-minute timeouts. After each job completes, verify row counts in the output CSV and confirm device name is logged. T2.1 runs seed 42 and T2.2 runs seed 123 sequentially on the shared GPU.

agents.name: Statistician
agents.instructions: You conduct statistical analysis of experimental results. Merge CSV files, compute augmentation benefit Δ = acc_aug − acc_noaug per (size,seed) combination, and fit an OLS log-linear regression Δ = a + b·log₂(N). Compute bootstrap (5000 iterations) confidence intervals for the crossover N* = 2^(−a/b). Run Spearman rank correlation for monotonicity testing. Flag any negative Δ values and report whether R² < 0.5 or N* falls outside the tested range. Save all numerical results to structured JSON and CSV files for downstream use.

agents.name: Visualization Engineer
agents.instructions: You produce publication-quality figures and summary documents. Use matplotlib and seaborn to create: per-size training/validation curve panels (7 sizes, 2-panel each, both seeds plus mean), a main Δ-vs-log(N) figure with regression line and CI band annotated with N*, and a grouped bar chart of final test accuracy. Save all figures as PNG at ≥150 dpi. The final output is results/SUMMARY.md containing all key numerical results in structured markdown format for the report writer.

summary: Five focused agents execute eleven tasks across four phases. A1 (ML Engineer) and A2 (Data Engineer) work in parallel to freeze the training codebase and generate stratified subset indices. A3 (GPU Training Engineer) then submits two sequential CUDA GPU jobs—seed 42 then seed 123—each training 14 CNN configurations (7 sizes × 2 augmentation conditions) for 5 epochs and saving per-epoch metrics to CSV. A4 (Statistician) merges results, computes augmentation benefit Δ per training size, fits a log-linear OLS regression, estimates the crossover N* with bootstrap CIs, and runs monotonicity diagnostics. A5 (Visualization Engineer) produces all publication PNG figures and the results/SUMMARY.md, with training-curve plots starting as soon as results are merged and the main Δ-vs-size figure following regression completion.

datasets.name: Fashion-MNIST
datasets.notes: 60,000 training + 10,000 test 28×28 grayscale images, 10 clothing categories. ~30 MB compressed. Normalisation: mean=0.2860, std=0.3530 from full training set. Direct S3: http://fashion-mnist.s3-website.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/
datasets.format: IDX binary (gzip), automatically decoded by torchvision into tensors
datasets.access_method: torchvision.datasets.FashionMNIST(root='data/', train=True, download=True) auto-downloads from S3 endpoint; no authentication required

checkpoints.reason: Human verifies data/class_balance_check.txt confirms ±1 per-class balance at N=500 and that subset_indices.npz contains all 28 expected keys before expensive GPU training begins

Human reviews analysis/delta_by_size.csv (augmentation benefit per size), analysis/regression_results.json (N* estimate and R²), and analysis/trend_diagnostics.txt (Spearman ρ, concordance) before publication figures and SUMMARY.md are finalized

execution_notes: T2.1 and T2.2 share a single GPU and run sequentially (T2.2 depends_on T2.1 for ordering); an agent may alternatively pack both seeds into one run_gpu_jobs call within T2.1 to save GPU startup overhead, then have T2.2 perform CPU-side verification only.
All figures are saved as PNG at ≥150 dpi (not PDF); the approved plan mentions PDF but the blueprint requires PNG for publication figures.
src/train_fmnist.py must be importable from the GPU job environment; the GPU job script must pip-install torch and torchvision internally since the GPU runs a fresh workspace copy.
Normalization statistics are fixed at mean=0.2860, std=0.3530 and must NOT be recomputed per subset to avoid data leakage; they are hardcoded in config.json and get_transforms().
If N* bootstrap CI is very wide or N_star_note is 'extrapolated', results/SUMMARY.md must state this clearly and T4.2 should skip the N* vertical annotation line.
T5.1 (paper writing) is excluded per blueprint rules; results/SUMMARY.md from T4.3 provides all structured inputs for the subsequent Report stage.
GPU timeout is 90 minutes per job; estimated actual runtime is 45–60 minutes per seed batch on T4/L4 at Fashion-MNIST scale with 14 runs.
No specialty binaries or MATLAB equivalents required; the entire pipeline uses pip-installable Python packages only.

T3.1 now reads results/gpu_log_seed42.txt and results/gpu_log_seed123.txt (both outputs of T2.1 and T2.2 respectively, which T3.1 depends on) and writes the device names to analysis/gpu_device_info.txt, which T4.3 then reads as a formal declared input. This ensures the dependency graph formally guarantees GPU device info is available to T4.3.
